newsitem.title: New Zealand: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 6.

text.p: My future is in the hands of my leader -- Morgan: NZ First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan was clinging to his job on Thursday night after admitting misleading leader Winston Peters over an attempt to get payment for television interviews. Page 1.

More than 200 air views on building: More than 200 public submissions have been received by the select committee hearing evidence on the petition oppposing a new $94 million ministerial building -- most of them against the proposal. Page 2.

Official papers destroyed -- report: Prime Minister Jim Bolger is surprised by a report that Cabinet ministers have instructed public servants to destroy documents because of fears that details would be revealed under the Official Information Act, his office says. Page 2.

Savings compulsion 'an abuse of power': The Stock Exchange has accused the government of an abuse of power in a submission to the Treasury-based group designing the compulsory savings scheme to be put into a referendum in September. Page 11.

Dairy Board to build $21m factory in China: The Dairy Board is building a $21 million factory in China as the basis of a projected $50 million consumer products business it plans to develop during the next five years there. Page 11.
Call for tight lead on NZ pit bull owners: All American pit bull terrier-type dogs should be classified as dangerous dogs, a parliamentary working group has recommended. Page 1.
Earnest Adams defers payout: Earnest Adams has yet to decide on declaring a dividend after releasing its annual result on Thursday. Page 16.
Mainfreight powers ahead to beat prospectus forecasts: Mainfreight has beaten prospectus forecasts and lifted its profit by a quarter despite the slowing economy. Page 16.

Email's NZ sales up 20pc: Australian whiteware manufacturer Email said on Thursday that its New Zealand sales had grown more than 20 percent to an annual NZ$35 million in the year ended March 31. Page 17.
An underground coalmine in Huntly is set to close in a surprise decision by owners Solid Energy. Page 1.

Placement angers Guardian: A $20 million diluting placement by Shortland Properties is upsetting one locked-out institutional shareholder. By placing shares at a discount, existing shareholders were giving away value, Guardian Trust said. Business section page 1.
